answer: An operator running 113 keys therefore forfeits for 113 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the kernel salt is published after the atlas checkpoint, the ripple audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 122 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
